title: Diverse Molecular Mechanisms Underlying Pathogenic Protein Mutations: Beyond the Loss-of-Function Paradigm.
journal: Annual review of genomics and human genetics
one_liner_zh: 综述致病突变通过改变蛋白互作、亲和力、特异性及促进聚集和相分离等非功能缺失机制致病的分子机制，虽非聚焦IDP且无AI/物理方法，但系统梳理了互作机制与相分离背景，对本课题机制建模有启发。
abstract: Most known disease-causing mutations occur in protein-coding regions of DNA. While some of these involve a loss of protein function (e.g., through premature stop codons or missense changes that destabilize protein folding), many act via alternative molecular mechanisms and have dominant-negative or gain-of-function effects. In nearly all cases, these non-loss-of-function mutations can be understood by considering interactions of the wild-type and mutant protein with other molecules, such as proteins, nucleic acids, or small ligands and substrates. Here, we review the diverse molecular mechanisms by which pathogenic mutations can have non-loss-of-function effects, including by disrupting interactions, increasing binding affinity, changing binding specificity, causing assembly-mediated dominant-negative and dominant-positive effects, creating novel interactions, and promoting aggregation and phase separation. We believe that increased awareness of these diverse molecular disease mechanisms will lead to improved diagnosis (and ultimately treatment) of human genetic disorders.
abstract_zh: 大多数已知的致病突变发生在DNA的蛋白质编码区。虽然其中一些涉及蛋白质功能的丧失（例如，通过提前终止密码子或导致蛋白质折叠不稳定的错义突变），但许多突变通过其他分子机制发挥作用，并具有显性负效应或功能获得效应。在几乎所有情况下，这些非功能丧失型突变都可以通过考虑野生型和突变型蛋白质与其他分子（如蛋白质、核酸或小配体和底物）的相互作用来理解。在此，我们回顾了致病突变产生非功能丧失效应的多种分子机制，包括破坏相互作用、增加结合亲和力、改变结合特异性、通过组装介导的显性负效应和显性正效应、创造新型相互作用，以及促进聚集和相分离。我们认为，对这些多样化分子疾病机制的认识加深将有助于改善人类遗传疾病的诊断（并最终实现治疗）。
